decisionsTitle: Automatic offers from the waiting list are a setting; «Trimite-i oferta» hands a place to a chosen person; newcomers queue while anyone waits (amending §104, §587, §589)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-01**, in his own words, as relayed with the request: «The option to auto-assign from the waiting list should be a config, because now if I increase the limits from 150 to 200 it will auto-draw from the waiting list, right?» · «Cumva vreau să pot aloca acele locuri preferențial, gen să aleg eu cui mai dau un loc» · «noi avem 200 de medalii (oficial am zis că sunt 150) dar cu marjă de eroare».

**The owner, 2026-10-01** (in three points, as relayed with the request): the race has **200 medals** and announces **150 places**, a margin the club keeps on purpose; once the waiting list forms, he wants to hand the places beyond 150 to the people he chooses rather than have them go to the head of the line the moment they exist; and the people who are waiting must not be overtaken by somebody who registers later.

### What happened until now

Every freed or added place went to the line at once. `fillAvailableSpots` is the one offering path: a cancellation, an offer's expiry or decline, an erasure, a late signature's release, the maintenance job's sweep — and the capacity raised in the editor (§147), which offers the new places **in order, at once, in the save's own transaction**. So raising 150 to 160 while ten people wait sends ten offers in the same second. «Dă-i un loc» (§67, §589, §592) seats one person on a paper declaration at the desk, into a place that is free under the lock; on an open race every free place had already been offered, so it met «full». There was no way to give a place to a chosen person by email.

### The decision

1. **The setting.** A column on the event, `events.waitlist_auto_offer boolean not null default true` (migration `0117`, expand-only): every existing event reads «Da», so nothing changes for the weekly run or the race until an organizer says so. In the editor's «Participare și înscrieri» box, under the capacity: «Ofertele din lista de așteptare pleacă automat» — «Da» / «Nu», with one sentence of help and the rest behind «?» (§511): on «Da» a place freed or added is offered at once to the first person waiting; on «Nu» places stay free until the organizer hands them out, from «Coada de înscrieri» with «Trimite-i oferta» or at the desk with «Dă-i un loc», and while anyone waits newcomers join the list too. A save that does not post the select changes nothing (the partners' discipline, §554). The series' scoped save carries it like the places (`SERIES_COLUMNS`), a copy and every date a series makes keep it, and every change writes `event.waitlist_auto_offer_changed` with `from` and `to` on each date it reached.
2. **One gate.** `fillAvailableSpots` offers nothing when the event's `waitlist_auto_offer` is false. The gate reads the column off the event's row inside the caller's transaction, after the caller took the event lock — so every caller obeys it with no check of its own and no caller's copy of the event can be stale. What `expireStaleHolds` released stays released: a lapsed offer or hold frees its place either way, and the place waits for the organizer. `findEventsNeedingMaintenance`'s free-place sweep also filters `waitlist_auto_offer = true`, so a manual event is not locked on every run to do nothing. Nothing else offers a place automatically. `domain/capacity.ts` is untouched.
3. **Newcomers queue while anyone waits.** In the allocator's opening (`placeForNewcomer`, shared by `allocateOrWaitlist` and a family's reservations), a new registration joins the waiting list whenever the event has a `WAITLISTED` row, even with a place free — under the same lock, from the count just taken (`domain/waitlist.ts#newcomerJoinsLine`). The §160 branch for a full line follows it too, so a full line with people waiting in it refuses rather than seating a newcomer past them. **An open offer is not somebody waiting** (§160's own reading): its holder already has a place, which the offer occupies, and a newcomer taking a *different* free place overtakes nobody. The request named open offers too; counting them was built and dropped, because it changes what «Da» does — the existing test of §160 (a full line's lapsed hold goes to the newcomer) failed, and a newcomer after a raise past the line was offered a place instead of holding one — while protecting nobody: once every waiting person has been offered, the places left over are open registration again under either reading, a day later at most. A family that arrives while anybody waits reserves nothing and joins the line whole once its address is confirmed (§543); a family that arrives with nobody waiting reserves as before.
4. **The public card and page.** While anybody waits (`waitlisted > 0`, or a cache entry's `waiting` from before the halves were counted — the same rule the allocator follows, so the door never promises what the press will not give), the open state no longer prints «N locuri libere din C»: it prints «**Locurile se dau din lista de așteptare** · M loc(uri) oferit(e) din lista de așteptare · N pe lista de așteptare» (the bold part, §472; the counts through `countForm`), and the door is the waiting list's — «Intră pe lista de așteptare», the hourglass, the same door the full state shows. The event page's `RegistrationCta` says the same line above that door, and no free-place count. With the line at its limit, or no list at all, the door is §348's refusal even with places free, since the newcomer would be refused at the end of the form. With nobody waiting — an open offer alone included — today's line and door, the offer named after the free places («2 locuri libere din 10 · 1 loc oferit din lista de așteptare», as this morning's section has it).
5. **«Trimite-i oferta».** A staff verb beside «Dă-i un loc» on the registration's own page, and on every waiting row of «Coada de înscrieri» on the event's page: `offerPlaceToByStaff`, modelled on `promoteFromWaitlistByStaff` up to the transition. Under the event lock it refuses a cancelled or finished event, expires the stale holds, requires `WAITLISTED`, refuses after the close (an offer then would be born lapsed — `OFFER_AFTER_CLOSE`, «La masă, folosește «Dă-i un loc».»), and requires a counted free place (`computeOccupied(counts) < capacity`, else §589's `NoFreePlaceError` and its sentence). Then it moves the row to `WAITLIST_OFFERED` with the ordinary deadline (`offerDeadline`: the club's hours, capped by the close and the start), queues the ordinary `WAITLIST_SPOT_OFFER` through the same function the automatic offer uses (`queueSpotOffer`, marked to leave now, §596), calls `fillAvailableSpots` once in the same transaction, as `promoteFromWaitlistByStaff` does (the stale-hold expiry above may have released another place; on «Nu» the gate makes it a no-op), writes `registration.offered_by_staff` (who, to whom, `aheadOf`: how many waited before them) in the offer's own transaction, and wakes the job for the deadline. It confirms nothing: the runner signs the declaration from the email. The Administrator's (`canManageRegistrations`, asserted in the action, the admin service and the service): «Dă-i un loc» is wider because the desk is every role's, but an offer changes a registration, which the Organizer reads and does not change (§289). The dialog: «Îi trimiți oferta?» — «{name} primește emailul «S-a eliberat un loc» și are până {deadline} să semneze; sare înaintea celor dinaintea lui.», the email's name and the deadline read from the catalogue and the event, in both languages. The «i» of §592 says why a press on a full event will be refused, as for «Dă-i un loc». A full event's refusal on the event's page names who holds the places, as on the registration's page.
6. **Nothing else moves.** «Dă-i un loc» stays the desk's paper confirmation into a free place — the verb for a walk-in, and for after the close. The automatic offer's order (oldest first) stays. Cancellation, expiry and erasure still release through the allocator.

**The recipe for the race.** Keep the capacity at 150 with «Da». When the list forms, set «Nu», raise the places by as many as you are about to hand out (not straight to 200), then send the offers one by one with «Trimite-i oferta»; walk-ins on the morning get «Dă-i un loc». Mind the end of the line: once nobody is `WAITLISTED` (an open offer does not count), the places still free go to whoever registers next, so raising 150 to 200 with ten waiting offers all ten and leaves forty open to the next newcomers. Written into `SETUP.md` §39 beside the capacity.

### Why one gate inside `fillAvailableSpots`

It is already the one path every freed or added place takes (§10.6); a check at each caller would be six checks that drift, and a caller added later would offer by default. Reading the column under the caller's lock makes the setting changed a moment ago the one obeyed.

### Why newcomers queue unconditionally

With automatic offers on it is almost never visible — a freed place is offered in the transaction that frees it, so nobody is left waiting beside a free place; the visible case is the desk after the close, when no offer is made and a walk-in now queues behind the people waiting (the desk's «Dă-i un loc» seats whoever the volunteer chooses). With offers off it is the rule that keeps the queue honest: a place the organizer has not handed out yet is not the next stranger's. One rule for both values is one rule to test.

### Why the card stops advertising free places while anyone waits

A newcomer cannot take them: the button would lead to the waiting list whatever the count said. «2 locuri libere din 10» beside «1 pe lista de așteptare» is what the owner's screenshot showed this morning (the section before this one); the card now says how places are given, and the door is the line's.

### The rules kept

No overbooking: a staff offer, like the automatic one, is made only under the event lock into a counted free place, and the offer occupies it (`countOccupied` counts an open offer), so a second press for the same place meets the full count. A new concurrency case in `tests/concurrency/capacity.test.ts`: offers by hand, one free place, two staff offers racing on two connections for two different people — exactly one is made, the other refused with `NoFreePlaceError`, one trail row. `kind` is in no new condition (a TEST registration is offered exactly as a REAL one, tested). Staff never bypass the declaration: an offer still needs the runner's signature.

*Rejected:*
- **An organizers' reserve inside the capacity formula** (places counted as held by the club). It would change the one formula every count reads (§10.6). Named as the follow-up if raising the capacity after the list forms proves clumsy.
- **A club-wide setting.** A race and a weekly run differ; the weekly run keeps offering on its own.
- **Letting newcomers take free places while people wait.** A queue nobody can trust.
- **A staff offer without a free place.** Overbooking by promise: two people told «the place is yours» for one place.

**Consequences.** Migration `0117_waitlist_auto_offer`; `db/schema/events.ts`; `registrations/service.ts` (`fillAvailableSpots`' gate, `placeForNewcomer`, the §160 branch, `queueSpotOffer`, `offerPlaceToByStaff`); `registrations/repository.ts` (`offersWaitlistAutomatically`, the sweep's filter); `registrations/domain/waitlist.ts` (`newcomerJoinsLine`, `OFFER_AFTER_CLOSE`); `registrations/admin-service.ts#offerPlaceByStaff`; `admin/registrations/actions.ts#offerPlaceAction` (back to the event's page from the queue); `registrations/give-place-tip.ts#offerDeadlineIfMadeNow`; `ui/OfferPlaceButton.tsx`, `ui/QueuePanel.tsx`, the registration's page, the event's page; `content/events` (fields, the save, the series, the copy, the trail, `RegistrationBox`); `events/domain/registration-cta.ts` (`fromWaitlist`), `RegistrationDoorButton`, `CardRegistration`, `RegistrationCta`; audit actions `registration.offered_by_staff`, `event.waitlist_auto_offer_changed`; `messages/{ro,en}.json`. Tests: `integration/registrations/waitlist-offers-setting.test.ts` (new), `integration/cms/capacity-raise.test.ts`, `integration/registrations/card-registration.test.ts`, `unit/events/registration-cta.test.ts`, `unit/events/card-registration-line.test.ts`, `concurrency/capacity.test.ts`, `unit/shared/confirmed-actions.test.ts`, `unit/shared/action-icons.test.ts`, `unit/shared/form-constraints.test.ts`, `unit/registrations/single-row-test-kind-email.test.ts`. No dependency.

### After review: the two doors that disagreed, and the recipe

- **The submit-time check follows the allocator.** `assertWaitlistCanTakeOneMore` returns on direct availability only when nobody waits (`!newcomerJoinsLine`), as `placeForNewcomer` does: with «Nu», a full line and the places raised above it, the form refuses WAITLIST_FULL before any email, rather than sending a confirmation the allocator would refuse.
- **The registration form asks the card's question.** `newcomerWouldQueue` (`events/domain/registration-cta.ts`) — no free place, or somebody WAITLISTED (the line's length for an older cache entry) — chooses the form page's waiting-list notice, with the offer hours, or its WAITLIST_FULL / NO_WAITLIST refusal, so someone arriving from «Intră pe lista de așteptare» on an open event is told what the list is.
- **The recipe warns of the end of the line.** Once everybody waiting has been offered nobody is WAITLISTED (an open offer does not count), and the free places go to whoever registers next: raise the places by as many as are about to be handed out (`SETUP.md` §39). Whether open offers should count as waiting stays the owner's question.
- **A staff offer sweeps what its own expiry released.** `offerPlaceToByStaff` ends with `fillAvailableSpots` in its transaction, so on «Da» a second lapsed hold freed by the same expiry is offered to the next in line at once rather than at the maintenance job's next sweep; on «Nu» the place stays free. Tested with two lapsed holds and two waiting, both settings.
- **Open question for the owner, before the race recipe is used:** `newcomerJoinsLine` counts only `WAITLISTED` rows, so once every waiting person has been offered, the places still free are open to the next newcomer. Should an open offer count as somebody waiting? Built and dropped (§3 above); his word decides.
changelogLine: - **You choose who gets a freed place** — each event says whether freed or added places are offered automatically to the waiting list; with that off, the organizer sends the offer to the person of their choice («Trimite-i oferta»), newcomers keep queueing while anyone waits, and the card says places are given from the waiting list instead of counting them free. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Each internal event carries «Ofertele din lista de așteptare pleacă automat» (`events.waitlist_auto_offer`, default true; the editor's registration box, carried by a series' scoped save, every change audited with from and to). With it false, `fillAvailableSpots` offers nothing — read off the event's row under the caller's lock, so a cancellation, an erasure, an offer's expiry, a capacity raise and the maintenance job all free places and offer nobody — and the maintenance job's free-place sweep does not select the event; with it true everything is as before (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given an event with at least one `WAITLISTED` registration, when a new registration is allocated — a confirmed address, a restart, a late signature, the desk, a family's form — then it joins the waiting list even while a place is free, under the event lock and whatever the event's automatic-offer setting; a family that arrives while anybody waits reserves nothing. An open offer is not somebody waiting: with nobody `WAITLISTED`, a newcomer takes a free place as before, a full line's lapsed hold included (§160). The form's own first check at submit refuses WAITLIST_FULL under the same rule — a full line with places free is refused before any email — and the registration form page shows the waiting-list notice or refusal by the card's rule (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

«Trimite-i oferta» on a waiting registration (its page and each waiting row of «Coada de înscrieri») is the Administrator's: under the event lock it refuses a cancelled or finished event, a registration that is not `WAITLISTED`, a closed registration (`OFFER_AFTER_CLOSE`) and an event with no counted free place (§589's sentence); otherwise it makes the ordinary offer to that person — not the oldest — with the ordinary deadline and `WAITLIST_SPOT_OFFER` email, confirms nothing, and, in the same transaction, offers any other place its expiry released to the next in line when the event offers automatically (a no-op on «Nu»), and writes `registration.offered_by_staff` naming who, to whom and how many waited before them. Two offers for one free place, in sequence or racing on two connections, make exactly one (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

While anybody waits (a `WAITLISTED` registration), an open event's card and page do not count places free: they say «Locurile se dau din lista de așteptare» / "Places are given from the waiting list", then the offered places and the people waiting, and offer the waiting list's door («Intră pe lista de așteptare»); with the line at its limit the door is the refusal of §348; with nobody waiting — an open offer alone included — the free places, the offer named after them, and the register button as before — in both languages, whatever the automatic-offer setting (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: automatic waiting-list offers as a setting, and offers by choice
